agent_2.name: Lucas
agent_2.occupation: software engineer and boyfriend of Sophia

metadata.scenario_context: Sophia has been promoted to the position of a Team Manager at her workplace, and her friends are throwing her a surprise party to celebrate her accomplishment.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Lucas, I was thinking... for Sophia's surprise party, what do you think about getting her yellow flowers as a gift? They seem cheerful and fitting for her accomplishment. 

Also, I've been wondering... do you strongly agree that making our parents proud should be one of our main goals in life?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
Yellow flowers could be nice... but I think something more personal might be better. Maybe a framed photo of us or a custom piece of jewelry? It shows more thought. 

As for making our parents proud, yes, I do strongly believe that. It's important to me. They sacrificed a lot for us, and I want to honor that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message:
I get that you want to honor your parents, but I don't really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it's all the same—people figure it out in their own ways. I mean, live and let live, right? 

But going back to Sophia, I still think yellow flowers would be a lovely touch. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Lucas
turns.message:
I get your point, but I still feel a more personal gift would mean more to Sophia, you know? Flowers are nice, but they'll wilt. Something lasting could really show how much we appreciate her.

And about making our parents proud, it’s just fundamental for me. It’s not just about living and letting live; it's about carrying on their legacy.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mark
turns.message:
I understand you value personal gifts, but flowers can carry a different kind of meaning. They can represent joy, celebration, and new beginnings, which fits Sophia perfectly. 

As for the whole making parents proud thing... I just can't see it that way. We all have our paths, right? I mean, what matters is how we feel about our own lives and choices, isn't it? Anyway, back to Sophia—those yellow flowers could really brighten her day.
